findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set. However, `getId()` returns the internal ID of the authorization resource entity in the policy store, not the group ID. In V2, resources are named by the group ID (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name). The V1 implementation correctly extracts the group ID from the resource name (`resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`). The fix should be `granted.add(groupResource.getName())`. This bug causes the group-based user visibility filtering to silently fail: the session attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` will contain meaningless authorization resource IDs instead of actual group IDs, so no users will match the group filter.

findings.title: canManage() grants manage access with only VIEW permission on all groups
findings.body: The no-argument `canManage()` method checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a user with only VIEW permission on the all-groups resource would pass the `requireManage()` check. This method gates group creation in `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()`. In contrast, `canManage(GroupModel group)` correctly checks only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`. A user who should only be able to view groups would be able to create new top-level groups. If this is intentional, the Javadoc on the interface should clarify the rationale; otherwise, the VIEW scope should be removed from this check.
